summary: Iteration 7 — Prompt 3 Student Master validation. Regression (Prompts 0/1/2): 72/72 green in ~13s. Added /app/backend/tests/test_student_master.py with 17 tests covering Student CRUD, duplicate/force, pagination/search/filter, PATCH, status change, enrollments (dup active year 409, snapshot update, patch), Guardian CRUD/search, student-guardian link/dup/unlink, Family CRUD+detail, shared-guardian-across-siblings, idempotent conversion, cross-tenant 404 (all endpoints), teacher RBAC 403, and audit-event coverage. 13/17 passed. 4 tests fail with the SAME root cause: MongoDB duplicate-key error on the sparse compound index (tenant_id, student_number) when inserting a Student whose `student_number` field is missing — MongoDB compound-sparse indexes include documents where ANY indexed field is present, so two students with tenant_id set + student_number missing collide with each other on `student_number: null`. This blocks (a) creating a second student with force=true, (b) all admission→student conversions after the first, (c) shared-guardian sibling flow, and (d) idempotent-conversion assertion. Frontend: login → /school lands; sidebar Student Master group shows sch-nav-students / sch-nav-guardians / sch-nav-families; /school/students renders students-page + students-table + btn-new-student and the new-student dialog contains all required testids (st-first, st-last, st-dob, st-gender, st-class, st-ay, st-submit); /school/guardians and /school/families both render with their -page/-table testids.

critical.issue: 500 Internal Error — pymongo DuplicateKeyError E11000 on index tenant_id_1_student_number_1 with `student_number: null`. Root cause: db.students index is declared sparse in /app/backend/app/core/db.py, but MongoDB *compound* sparse indexes include docs where at least one indexed field is present (tenant_id is), so two docs missing `student_number` both index as null and collide. All Student rows omit `student_number` (only `admission_number` is written), so ANY tenant that already has one student cannot receive a second student via /students or /convert.

action_items: CRITICAL: Fix the students collection unique index so a missing `student_number` does not trigger E11000. Two viable fixes: (a) replace `sparse=True` with `partialFilterExpression={'student_number': {'$exists': True}}` on the (tenant_id, student_number) unique index; or (b) drop that index entirely (only `admission_number` is used by new code — student_number is a legacy Prompt-2 field). Apply the same partialFilter treatment to (tenant_id, admission_number) for safety. Existing index will need to be manually dropped and recreated (Mongo silently no-ops create_index when a same-name index already exists with different options).

After fixing the index, re-run: `pytest /app/backend/tests/test_student_master.py -v` — expect all 17 green including test_12_duplicate_force_bypasses, test_20_list_pagination_and_search (depends on force insert), test_90_shared_guardian_across_siblings, and test_91_idempotent_conversion_second_call.
Consider migrating the new-student dialog DOB input from native <input type=date> to the shadcn Calendar/Popover used in the admissions dialog for consistency.
critical_code_review_comments: conversion.py correctly reuses existing guardian by (tenant_id, mobile_primary) — semantics match the sibling-sharing requirement. Idempotency check via existing admission_conversion row + app.status==CONVERTED is sound. However this test could not verify runtime behavior because insert_one on students fails first.

student_routes.py: duplicate_student check uses regex `^{name}$` on user-provided input without re-escaping — special regex characters in a real name (e.g., `O'Brien`, dots, parens) could either crash or produce false negatives. Prefer case-insensitive collation or `re.escape`.
Student model has `student_code` but no `student_number` field — the db.py index on `student_number` is dead code that only creates bugs. Remove it.
In list_students & list_guardians, `q` regex is also unescaped — same injection/false-match risk.

student_routes.py returns raw `_out(doc)` for student creation, which includes `student_number: null` implicitly? No — `to_mongo(exclude_none=True)` strips it, so the response is fine. But this confirms the index-vs-payload mismatch.

New test_student_master.py (17 tests) has 4 failures all caused by the SAME MongoDB index bug — fix (tenant_id, student_number) unique index using partialFilterExpression or drop it. Note: the DEV MongoDB may need the stale non-partial index manually dropped: `db.students.dropIndex('tenant_id_1_student_number_1')` before startup recreates it correctly. rca of the issue: MongoDB compound sparse indexes index a document whenever *any* of the indexed fields is present. The students collection has a `(tenant_id, student_number)` unique+sparse index. New Student inserts omit `student_number` (the Student pydantic model doesn't define it, and to_mongo() uses exclude_none=True). Because tenant_id is always present, each such doc is indexed with `student_number: null`. Two docs in the same tenant → E11000. Reproduction: (1) POST /school/students {first_name:'X', force:true} — first succeeds, second returns 500. (2) POST /convert on two approved applications in the same tenant — second returns 500. Fix: replace sparse=True with partialFilterExpression={'student_number': {'$exists': True}} in /app/backend/app/core/db.py (line 72), OR remove the index — Student model no longer uses student_number, only admission_number. Then manually drop the pre-existing non-partial index in Mongo and let startup recreate.
